title: Chevron Confirms West Texas Power Project for Microsoft Is on Schedule
summary:
The energy company expects to deliver its first electricity to a new West Texas facility by 2028, following an update from its chief financial officer. Chevron stated that the natural gas power project intended for a Microsoft data center is proceeding as planned and should be fully operational by 2031.

The timeline remains firm despite a decision by Texas Governor Greg Abbott to pause permits for new digital infrastructure in the state. The update came during a review of the oil major's third-quarter results, which showed revenue of $67.80B, exceeding the $61.62B expected by analysts.

CHEVRON $CVX SAYS ITS MICROSOFT $MSFT DATA CENTER POWER PROJECT IN WEST TEXAS IS STILL ON SCHEDULE

That's despite Texas Governor Greg Abbott pausing permits for new data centers, per Bloomberg.

Chevron will supply natural gas to power the project. Its CFO says Chevron still expects first power in 2028 and a full ramp-up by 2031.
